source.original_title: 05/18/2026 - Mike Bennett x Harry Edmonds KL
source.display_title: 05/18/2026 - Mike Bennett x Harry Edmonds KL — Lost

setter.name: Kyla
setter.evidence: Rep: 'I know you spoke with Kyla. Um, she gave me like a bit of a background, so I've kind of got a head start.' Prospect independently: 'it must have submitted a partial whatever and then Kyla reached out.' Both parties name her and the rep uses 'she', unlike his references to Kim.

prospect.name: Mike Bennett
prospect.location: San Diego, California, USA — mid-move to Connecticut, house in packing boxes at the time of the call
prospect.occupation: Consultant; was also attempting to start a woodworking business
prospect.training_background: Extensive and highly self-directed. Daily: meditation, a nine-minute warm-up in place of coffee, the five Tibetan rites at 21 reps each, and a five-round readiness circuit of roughly 30 push-ups, 150 crunches, 30 alternating curls, 30 diamond push-ups, 50 leg lifts and 50 bodyweight squats. Twice weekly full-body dumbbell work up to 50 lb using a 4:0:1:0 tempo to extract more from limited load. Peloton once or twice a week, walking four to five times a week, running twice a week while training for a 5k and a triathlon, and hiking five to ten miles weekly with a 20 lb rucksack every other weekend. Owns several maces. Was formerly a lot more overweight. The resistance and running components had been on hold for about six weeks due to the move.
prospect.medical: Repeated cycles of burnout described as systemic overload — about a year ago he could not train on consecutive days without being 'tanked' for two or three days. Has been on the Bean Protocol for roughly a year, a strict elimination diet with staged reintroduction, working with a Bean Protocol specialist. Developed a dependency on 'Feel Free', a kava-kratom product, which he says contributed to a further burnout and severely disrupted his sleep; he stopped in November after repeated attempts to moderate. Only began sleeping through the night again about two weeks before the call, having previously woken at one to three in the morning for two to four hours. Self-assesses at roughly 80% of baseline. Tracks recovery on a wearable, reporting a 93 readiness and 93 sleep score.

signals: Highly self-directed and capable, running an elaborate self-designed regimen and sourcing programming free: 'I'm picking up stuff on Instagram. So it's like, I'm doing all right.'
Skepticism is the defining feature and it is aimed at the product claim itself: 'I've never seen anybody that only spends 20 to 30 minutes in the gym, or whatever, looking like that'
Anchored to an alternative that is genuinely working — sleep restored, protocol adherence, wearable scores in the nineties
The bargain half of the label is untested rather than confirmed: no price objection arose because the rep disqualified before any negotiation. He was told the price and did not react to it at all

goals.text: More variety in his training rather than sticking to the same movements
Better efficiency and effectiveness from the time he already spends training
An overall overhaul of his approach with better methods
Continue climbing back to full baseline after repeated burnout

pains.text: Repeated cycles of burnout and systemic overload; at one point could not train on consecutive days without being wiped out for days
Dependency on a kava-kratom product he repeatedly failed to moderate, which he says caused a further burnout and wrecked his sleep from around September until he stopped in November
Insomnia — waking at one to three in the morning for two to four hours; only resolved about two weeks before the call
Stuck in the same routines and wants variety; suspects he is leaving effectiveness on the table
Resistance training and running on hold for about six weeks with no gym access during a cross-country move
Was trying to run a consulting practice and start a woodworking business simultaneously and found it too much
Doubts the core product claim is achievable — 'the dude is pretty ripped, his chest is huge... I've never seen anybody that only spends 20 to 30 minutes in the gym looking like that'

objections.raw_quote: I mean, the dude is pretty ripped, his chest is huge, pumping out, you know, it's like, I've never seen anybody that only spends 20 to 30 minutes in the gym, or whatever, looking like that.
objections.rep_response: Asked the right opening probe — 'What's got you skeptical?' — but did not answer the doubt. He replied 'Interesting. I'm not saying it's not. Yeah, no, no, I'm curious' and pivoted to asking how long the prospect currently trains for, asserting only that 'that's what we'll be getting to do. 30 minutes, 45 max.' No evidence, no client results, no explanation of why the volume works.

objections.raw_quote: to be honest, And be honest, the truth is I didn't actually complete the application. I skipped a couple of questions and I got to the end and I'm like, I don't know if I want to do this and I was going to go back and answer and I just was like, okay, I'm not going to do that right now. And it must have submitted a partial whatever and then Kyla reached out. So that's like, I, I was sort of on the fence myself.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it and disqualified transparently rather than pushing: named the ICP, named the price, and explicitly declined to sell. 'typically people who would do this program are people who really want to go from good to great... It's six grand for six months... if you don't feel like you're necessarily ready for it, fine. You know, I'm not going to sit here and push it onto you.'

evidence: The rep disqualified rather than the prospect declining: 'It sounds like you kind of, you've got a lot of things in place, nutrition-wise, sleep-wise, you're training, you know?... It doesn't really sound like we can do too much for you'
Rep then declined to sell explicitly: 'if you don't feel like you're necessarily ready for it, fine. You know, I'm not going to sit here and push it onto you'
Prospect confirmed he had never intended to apply: 'I didn't actually complete the application... I don't know if I want to do this'
No offer walkthrough, no pillars presented, no close attempted, no payment discussed beyond the price being named once in the disqualification

Counter-evidence for reading this as follow_up instead: the rep left a door open and shared his number — 'if you do feel like you do want to talk about it, hit me up. If not, that's fine' — and the prospect replied 'it gives me a lot to think about.' There is no scheduled next step, no commitment and no stated intention to return, so lost is the honest read, but the confidence is held at 0.72 to reflect the open door
outcome.next_step: None scheduled. Rep to text his phone number and a written sleep protocol; prospect free to make contact if he changes his mind.

notable.note: Two findings worth a principal's attention. First, the lead was manufactured: the prospect abandoned the application deliberately, a partial submission was captured anyway, and the setter called him on it. He said so unprompted — 'I got to the end and I'm like, I don't know if I want to do this... And it must have submitted a partial whatever and then Kyla reached out.' Any call rate computed over booked calls is being diluted by prospects who chose not to apply. Second, and to the rep's credit, this is the clearest good-conduct example in the batch: presented with a fit-poor lead he named the ICP, named the price, and explicitly refused to push. It stands in direct contrast to the Peter Louis call earlier the same day, where a comparable self-sufficiency objection was met with a cascade of cheaper options. Also of note, the prospect's skepticism was in substance a doping insinuation about the founder — that nobody training 20 to 30 minutes a day looks like that — and it was never answered.

quality.notes: The opening sixteen seconds are fully inverted: the relocation from San Diego to Connecticut and the boxes belong to the prospect, not the rep, who is confirmed London-based across every other call in this folder. The block at 00:07:37 is labelled as the rep and correctly contains the rep's disqualification, but the surrounding short turns alternate unreliably, and the sleep-advice exchange from 00:10:26 to 00:11:46 has the rep's protocol landing under both labels. Roles read from content throughout.
